# F13 — Agent profiles

Settings → Agent is a library of named agent profiles. Each profile is either an
OpenHands agent (an LLM profile, a system prompt, a tool set, parallel
tool calls, and MCP-server and secret scopes) or an ACP external agent (a preset
such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Pi or OpenCode, its launch command, a
model the agent itself reports, and provider credentials). One profile is
active; new conversations started from Home launch from it.

Source: `src/routes/agent-profiles-settings.tsx`, `src/routes/agent-settings.tsx`, `src/components/features/settings/agent-profiles/`, `src/components/features/settings/acp-credentials-section.tsx`, `src/components/features/settings/acp-conflict-warnings.tsx`, `src/components/features/settings/acp-auth-status-banner.tsx`, `src/constants/acp-providers.ts`, `src/constants/acp-brand-marks.ts`, `src/hooks/query/use-acp-model-discovery.ts`, `src/hooks/mutation/use-create-conversation.ts`, `src/hooks/mutation/resolve-conversation-launch.ts`, `src/hooks/mutation/use-new-conversation-command.ts`.

## Sub-features

- `F13.list`: under **Available Profiles**, rows (sorted by name) show the profile name, then its LLM profile (OpenHands) or `ACP (external subprocess)`, a **Default** badge on the active profile and a `...` menu (Edit, Set as active, Delete).
- `F13.create`: **Add agent profile** opens the editor; Save toasts `Profile "<name>" created` and the row is listed after a reload.
- `F13.name-validation`: an empty or malformed name marks the field invalid (red rule) and disables Save; a name another profile already has also marks the field invalid, shows a red taken-name message about agent profiles under it (the rule stays grey) and disables Save (Edit accepts the profile's own name).
- `F13.editor-no-llm`: with no LLM profiles, an OpenHands profile shows `Create an LLM profile first to define an OpenHands agent.` and Save toasts `Select an LLM profile for this agent.` without creating anything.
- `F13.openhands-options`: OpenHands profiles offer an LLM profile dropdown (the active LLM profile by default), a **System prompt** choice (`OpenHands default`, `Default + your instructions` or `Custom persona`, each saved on the profile), **Parallel tool calls** (default 1, minimum 1) and **Tools**: `Standard tools` (default) lists the server's standard set read-only, `Choose tools` turns the server's tool catalog into switches; values persist and reopen.
- `F13.edit`: Edit reopens the stored values with Save disabled until something changes; renaming keeps the profile id; Back and Cancel leave without saving.
- `F13.stale-llm-ref`: editing a profile whose LLM profile no longer exists preselects the active LLM profile and enables Save, so saving heals the reference; launching it unhealed on a backend advertising per-launch LLM override keeps the profile and runs the active LLM profile (`launched_agent_profile.llm_profile_ref`).
- `F13.set-active`: **Set as active** toasts `Switched to profile "<name>"`, moves the Default badge and is disabled on the active row.
- `F13.active-drives-conversation`: a conversation started from Home, or with `/new` typed in a conversation's composer, after activation launches from that profile (its id and settings are stamped on the conversation); with an ACP profile active, `/new` starts an ACP agent. The seeded OpenHands `default` launches from the global agent settings (no `launched_agent_profile`).
- `F13.llm-pill-precedence`: when the active profile pins a different LLM profile than the Home LLM pill, a backend advertising per-launch LLM override uses the pill's LLM while preserving the named profile's other settings and identity.
- `F13.mcp-scope`: **MCP servers** offers **All servers** (every configured server listed, switched on and disabled) or **Choose servers** (a switch per configured server); the choice persists; a chosen server that was removed stays listed with a red warning, and launching with it is refused.
- `F13.secrets-scope`: **Secrets** offers **No profile restriction** (every switch on and disabled) or **Choose secrets**; on an ACP profile, Choose preselects that provider's secret names; the selection persists.
- `F13.acp-form`: choosing **ACP (external subprocess)** shows Preset, Command, Credentials and Model; each preset prefills its command and its model choice (`Agent default`, or Gemini CLI's preferred `gemini-2.5-pro`), **Custom** empties the command and disables Save until one is typed, typing a preset's exact command selects that preset, and the Model list's **Custom** opens a free-text model field.
- `F13.acp-local-presets`: on a local backend the Preset list also offers **Pi** and **OpenCode** (with their own commands and credentials); a profile saved on them stores `acp_server` `pi`/`opencode` with `acp_command` `null`. On Cloud both are hidden (blocked here).
- `F13.acp-model-discovery`: for a built-in preset with its default command the Model list comes from the agent: `Asking <agent> which models it offers…` while the agent-server asks it, then its models with `Agent default (<model>)` first; an agent that wants a login says `Sign in or add credentials above to see the models <agent> offers.`, one that cannot start says `<agent>'s models appear here after your first conversation with it. …`; a picked model is saved as `acp_model` and reopens selected.
- `F13.acp-credentials`: built-in presets show a Credentials section (password fields), an auth banner (signed in / configured), a conflict warning for mutually exclusive Claude credentials, and `Already saved — leave blank to keep` for stored values. Credentials are saved as global secrets.
- `F13.acp-preset-credentials`: the Credentials fields follow the preset: Claude Code `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`; Codex `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `CODEX_AUTH_JSON` (multi-line), `OPENAI_BASE_URL`; Gemini CLI `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS_JSON` (multi-line), `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION`, `GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_BASE_URL`; Pi `PI_AUTH_JSON` (multi-line), `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; OpenCode `OPENCODE_AUTH_CONTENT` (multi-line), `OPENCODE_API_KEY`; **Custom** has no Credentials section. With no host login and no stored credential (Gemini here) no auth banner shows.
- `F13.menu-keyboard`: opening the row's `...` menu focuses Edit; ArrowDown/ArrowUp move focus between the enabled items (wrapping, and skipping the disabled **Set as active** on the active row), Enter runs the focused item, and Tab, Escape or a click outside close the menu.
- `F13.delete`: Delete asks for confirmation; Cancel keeps the row, Delete removes it. Deleting the active profile selects `default` immediately; deleting the last profile makes the server re-seed and activate `default`.
- `F13.phone`: the list, row menu and editor fit a 390 px viewport without horizontal overflow.
- `F13.acp-conversation`: a conversation launched from an active ACP profile runs the external agent. Blocked without an approved provider account.
- `F13.cloud-read-only`: on a Cloud backend, organization members see rows without the `...` menu or **Add agent profile**. Blocked without a Cloud account.

## How to get to it (user POV)

- Sidebar settings gear (`backend-selector-settings-link`): on desktop `/settings` redirects to `/settings/agents`. In the settings navigation, **Agent** (`sidebar-settings-/settings/agents`).
- Direct URL `/settings/agents`; the retired `/settings/agent` redirects there.
- Command menu (`Control+k`/`Meta+k` or `command-menu-trigger`): **Agent settings**.
- Getting-started checklist **Customize your agent** and the composer **+** → **Switch agent profile** → **Manage agent profiles** (both mapped in F09/F05).
- On Home, the composer **+** → **Switch agent profile** list activates a profile like **Set as active** (F05.agent-profile-switch).
- All per-profile actions are in the row's `...` menu (`agent-profile-menu-trigger`). The editor has no route: it replaces the list in place.

## Driving it with control-openhands

Preconditions:

- Baseline state (launched, doctored, `onboard --skip` done) on a **fresh** run. `F13.editor-no-llm` must run before `control-openhands llm preset deepseek`; everything from `F13.stale-llm-ref` on needs the preset (`deepseek-flash` active, `deepseek-pro`).
- A fresh run has one profile, `default`, active, whose LLM profile is `default` (which does not exist). `control-openhands api GET /api/agent-profiles` shows it.
- `F13.mcp-scope` needs two configured MCP servers. Arrange them with `control-openhands api POST /api/settings/mcp/qa_mcp_a --data '{"transport":"stdio","command":"qa-no-such-command","enabled":false}' --write` and the same for `qa_mcp_b`.
- `F13.acp-conversation` needs the provider's agent CLI and an approved account; `F13.cloud-read-only` needs a Cloud organization member login. Both are blocked here.
- Dropdowns are autocompletes. Pick an option with `control-openhands browser choose 'testid=<testid>' '<label>'` (proven on `agent-type-selector`, `agent-preset-selector`, `agent-model-selector` (`Custom`), `agent-profile-llm-selector`, `agent-settings-mcp-mode` and `agent-settings-secrets-mode`). The manual opener, `control-openhands browser click 'div:has(> div > input[data-testid=<testid>]) >> role=button[name="Show suggestions"]'` then `browser click 'role=option[name="<label>"]'`, works for most of them but is flaky right after an editor opens (see Gotchas); clicking the input itself can open an empty, filtered list.

- **List (`F13.list`).** From `/` run `control-openhands browser click 'testid=backend-selector-settings-link' --expect-url '/settings'`, then `control-openhands browser url` (`/settings/agents`) and `control-openhands browser text 'testid=agent-profile-row'`: `default`, its LLM profile `default`, `Default` on three lines. `control-openhands browser count 'testid=agent-profile-active-badge'` is `1`; `control-openhands browser screenshot --feature F13.list --name list`. Command menu: run `control-openhands browser goto /` (the browser is on `/settings/agents`, where the URL wait would pass at once), `control-openhands browser press Control+k`, `control-openhands browser type 'testid=command-menu >> role=combobox' 'Agent settings'`, `control-openhands browser press Enter`, `control-openhands browser wait-url '/settings/agents(\?|$)'`. Legacy URL: `control-openhands browser goto /settings/agent` returns `.../settings/agents`.
- **No LLM profile (`F13.editor-no-llm`).** Before the preset, run `control-openhands browser click 'testid=add-agent-profile'`, then `control-openhands browser text 'testid=agent-profile-no-llm'`: `Create an LLM profile first to define an OpenHands agent.` `control-openhands browser text 'testid=agent-profile-editor-title'` is `Add agent profile` and `control-openhands browser text 'testid=agent-profile-editor-description'` is `Configure the agent below, then click Save to create this profile.`. Run `control-openhands browser fill 'testid=agent-profile-name-input' QA_NoLlm`; Save turns enabled (`control-openhands browser enabled 'testid=save-agent-profile-btn'`). Click `testid=save-agent-profile-btn` and run `control-openhands browser toasts`: `Select an LLM profile for this agent.` `api GET /api/agent-profiles` lists no `QA_NoLlm`. Leave with `control-openhands browser click 'testid=cancel-agent-profile-btn'`.
- **Name rules (`F13.name-validation`).** In the Add editor, fill `testid=agent-profile-name-input` with `''`, `default`, `'bad name!'` and `QA_ok` in turn; after each run `control-openhands browser attr 'testid=agent-profile-name-input' aria-invalid` and `control-openhands browser enabled 'testid=save-agent-profile-btn'`. Results: `''` → `true`/`false`; `default` (duplicate) → `true`/`false`; `'bad name!'` → `true`/`false`; `QA_ok` → `false`/`true`. The rule under the field is always shown (grey) and turns the theme danger colour (`text-danger`, #18199) while the name is invalid; it reads `Profile name must start with a letter or digit, and contain only letters, digits, dots, underscores, or hyphens (max 64 characters)`. For the duplicate, `control-openhands browser count 'role=alert >> text=already exists'` is `1`: the alert is the field's description, in the danger colour (`rgb(231, 106, 94)` on OpenHands-Neutral, `rgb(209, 52, 56)` on Light+), while the rule text stays grey. It reads `An agent profile with this name already exists. Choose a different name, or edit the existing one.` Take `control-openhands browser screenshot --feature F13.name-validation --name duplicate` with `default` filled. In Edit the same message appears for another profile's name and not for the profile's own name (`F13.edit`).
- **ACP form (`F13.acp-form`).** In the Add editor run `control-openhands browser click 'testid=agent-type-selector'` and `control-openhands browser click 'role=option[name="ACP (external subprocess)"]'`. `control-openhands browser value 'testid=agent-preset-selector'` is `Claude Code`, `browser value 'testid=agent-command-input'` is `npx -y --prefer-offline @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp@0.63.0` and `browser value 'testid=agent-model-selector'` is `Agent default`; `agent-profile-no-llm` is gone (ACP needs no LLM profile). The preset list (`control-openhands browser click 'div:has(> div > input[data-testid=agent-preset-selector]) >> role=button[name="Show suggestions"]'`, then `control-openhands browser snapshot 'role=listbox'`) is `Claude Code`, `Codex`, `Gemini CLI`, `Pi`, `OpenCode`, `Custom` (`browser press Escape`). Pick `Codex` and `Gemini CLI` from `testid=agent-preset-selector`: the command becomes `npx -y --prefer-offline @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp@1.10.0` / `npx -y --prefer-offline @google/gemini-cli@0.46.0 --acp` and the model `Agent default` / `gemini-2.5-pro` (the models come from the agent since #18131: `F13.acp-model-discovery`). Pick `Custom`: the command is empty and Save is disabled. `control-openhands browser fill 'testid=agent-command-input' 'npx -y qa-custom-acp --stdio'` enables Save. Filling the exact Codex command flips the preset to `Codex`; appending ` --verbose` flips it back to `Custom`. Model override: with a built-in preset, run `control-openhands browser choose 'testid=agent-model-selector' 'Custom'` (or open the model list with its toggle button and `control-openhands browser click 'role=option[name="Custom"][exact]'`); `control-openhands browser count 'testid=agent-model-input'` is `1` and empty. The **Custom** preset shows `agent-model-input` directly (no model list).
- **Create an ACP profile (`F13.create`).** With preset `Custom`, fill `testid=agent-profile-name-input` with `QA_acp_custom`, `testid=agent-command-input` with `'npx -y qa-custom-acp --stdio'` and `testid=agent-model-input` with `qa-model`, click `testid=save-agent-profile-btn`, then `control-openhands browser wait-text 'Profile "QA_acp_custom" created' --timeout 10000`, `control-openhands browser reload` and `control-openhands browser text 'testid=agent-profile-row >> has-text=QA_acp_custom'`: `QA_acp_custom` / `ACP (external subprocess)`. `control-openhands api GET /api/agent-profiles/QA_acp_custom` shows `acp_server` `custom`, the command and `acp_model` `qa-model`.
- **Pi and OpenCode presets (`F13.acp-local-presets`).** For each of `OpenCode` and `Pi`: run `control-openhands browser click 'testid=add-agent-profile'`, `control-openhands browser choose 'testid=agent-type-selector' 'ACP (external subprocess)'` and `control-openhands browser choose 'testid=agent-preset-selector' '<preset>'`. `browser value 'testid=agent-command-input'` is `npx -y --prefer-offline opencode-ai@1.18.23 acp` / `npx -y --prefer-offline --package=pi-acp@0.0.33 --package=@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@0.83.0 pi-acp` (the versions follow `@openhands/typescript-client`). Fill `testid=agent-profile-name-input` with `QA_opencode` / `QA_pi`, run `control-openhands browser wait 'testid=agent-model-discovering' --state detached --timeout 120000`, click `testid=save-agent-profile-btn` and `control-openhands browser wait-text 'Profile "<name>" created' --timeout 10000`. `control-openhands api GET /api/agent-profiles/<name>` has `acp_server` `opencode` / `pi`, `acp_command` `null` and `acp_model` `null`, and after `browser reload` both rows read `<name>` / `ACP (external subprocess)`. Cloud hides both presets (blocked here: needs a Cloud backend).
- **Models from the agent (`F13.acp-model-discovery`).** In a new ACP editor, each built-in preset pick first shows (unless a successful lookup for that preset and secret set is cached, about 5 minutes: OpenCode then skips it) `control-openhands browser text 'testid=agent-model-discovering'` `Asking <agent> which models it offers…` (the agent-server runs the agent CLI through npx for `POST /api/acp/models`; the first lookup can take a minute while npx downloads it). Wait with `control-openhands browser wait 'testid=agent-model-discovering' --state detached --timeout 120000`, then read `control-openhands browser testids --hidden --filter agent-model`. In this sandbox (no Claude, Codex, Gemini or Pi login for the agent-server): Claude Code fails to start and shows `agent-model-list-after-first-conversation` (`Claude Code's models appear here after your first conversation with it. You can also switch models from the chat.`); Codex, Gemini CLI and Pi need a login and show `agent-model-discovery-needs-auth` (`Sign in or add credentials above to see the models <agent> offers.`), with the model left at `Agent default` (`gemini-2.5-pro` for Gemini); `<run>/private/stack.log` logs `ACP model discovery failed: server=<key> code=ACPInitError|ACPAuthRequired`. OpenCode needs no key: `browser value 'testid=agent-model-selector'` is `Agent default (OpenCode/Big Pickle)` and the list (open it with `browser click 'div:has(> div > input[data-testid=agent-model-selector]) >> role=button[name="Show suggestions"]'`, then `browser snapshot 'role=listbox'`) has that entry, a non-empty list of the models OpenCode reports live (12 on 2026-10-13, such as `OpenCode/Big Pickle` and `OpenCode/Exo Free`) and `Custom` (screenshot `--feature F13.acp-model-discovery --name opencode-models`). Edit `QA_opencode`: Save is disabled until `control-openhands browser choose 'testid=agent-model-selector' 'OpenCode/Exo Free'`; Save (`Profile "QA_opencode" updated`) stores `acp_model` `opencode/exo-free`, and reopening shows `OpenCode/Exo Free` with Save disabled. With a saved `OPENAI_API_KEY` (even a dummy, `F13.acp-credentials`) Codex lists its models and shows `Agent default (GPT-6-Astra)`. Lookups never add a conversation to the list (`api GET "/api/conversations/search?limit=20"` stays empty).

- **Pill wins over a pinned LLM (`F13.llm-pill-precedence`).** With `QA_oh` active (pinned to `deepseek-pro`) and the Home pill on `deepseek-flash` (`browser text 'testid=chat-input-llm-profile'` on `/`), run `control-openhands conversation start --prompt "Reply with only: qa-profile-ok. - **MCP scope (`F13.mcp-scope`).** With `qa_mcp_a` and `qa_mcp_b` arranged, `browser goto /settings/agents`, Edit `QA_oh`: `browser value 'testid=agent-settings-mcp-mode'` is `All servers` and the eval below (with `+(i.disabled?'(disabled)':'')` appended) shows both `=true(disabled)`. ## Gotchas

- The editor is not a route: `browser url` stays `/settings/agents` and `browser reload` drops unsaved edits back to the list. The settings page header (`settings-page-subtitle`) is hidden while it is open.
- Autocomplete dropdowns: clicking an input that already shows a value can open an empty listbox (the text filters it), and an option click then times out. The toggle-button opener does not always open the list either: on the Edit editor's `agent-profile-llm-selector` (bottom of the form) the option click timed out 5 of 5 times right after opening the editor, and the model list's `Custom` option once detached mid-click after a preset change. `browser choose` avoids the input-filtering problem, but an option may still remain unstable immediately after opening an editor. Reload and reopen before retrying; the suffix-identity check can use the already-selected active LLM without changing that dropdown. A listbox also closes if you spend a command (snapshot, eval) in between, so click the option right after opening.
- A taken name marks the field invalid with an alert reading `An agent profile with this name already exists. …`.
- `has-text=default` also matches the active row's `Default` badge (Playwright's text match ignores case), so with several profiles `'testid=agent-profile-row >> has-text=default'` hits two rows; select the seeded profile with `'testid=agent-profile-row >> nth=-1'` (it sorts last) or by its badge.
- Model lookups (`F13.acp-model-discovery`) spawn the provider CLI on the agent-server machine through npx with the profile's allowed secrets; they send no prompt. A failed lookup is retried each time the preset is picked again; a successful one is cached for about five minutes per preset and secret set.
- Switch rows are `sr-only` checkboxes inside labels (keyboard reachable): click the label text (`'testid=agent-settings-tool-list >> text=<tool>'`, `'testid=agent-settings-mcp-list >> text=<name>'`) and read `.checked` with `browser eval`. A bare `label` selector segment is parsed as `label=`, not CSS.
- The Default badge, the **Set as active** item and the `Switched to profile` toast all refer to the same active pointer; the wording differs from the LLM page (**Set as default**).
- The OpenHands row's grey text is the LLM profile name, not the kind. A fresh run's `default` shows `default` there although no LLM profile of that name exists until it is edited (`F13.stale-llm-ref`).
- Local seeded OpenHands `default` launches through global agent settings so the Skills selection applies; its per-profile fields do not apply on that path. Named profiles use their saved settings. Home launches follow the LLM pill. On a backend advertising per-launch LLM override, a named profile pinned to another LLM keeps its tool, concurrency and MCP settings; read `launched_agent_profile` and `agent` on the conversation (`F13.llm-pill-precedence`). The same override covers a named profile whose LLM reference no longer exists. Only older backends without that capability use the legacy settings fallback in those two cases. `/new` and local child conversations launch through the same path.
- The ACP auth probe runs the provider CLI on the agent-server machine. If that machine has a Claude CLI login, Claude Code can show "already signed in". Use only an explicitly approved account for authenticated ACP checks.
- ACP credentials are global secrets, not profile fields: cancelling the editor saves nothing, but saving any ACP profile with a typed credential writes it to Settings → Secrets (F14) for every conversation.
- **Choose secrets** on an ACP profile also selects provider secret names that are not saved (`CODEX_AUTH_JSON`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL`); they show as switches without descriptions.
- The empty state (`agent-profiles-empty`) and the load-error state (`agent-profiles-load-error`) are not reachable on a local backend: deleting the last profile re-seeds `default`, and with the agent-server stopped the app swaps to **Manage backends** after a reload, or keeps the cached list without one.
- The refused-launch toast text comes from the Agent Server and changes between versions (`MCP server(s) not configured: <name>` on 1.53.0): assert that one toast names the server and the prompt stays, not the exact wording.
- Opening a row menu focuses its first enabled item. Arrows skip disabled **Set as active**; Escape closes the menu and returns focus to its trigger, while Tab closes it and continues normal tab order.
- The Add agent editor has its own agent description. Parallel tool calls label and description are translated.
- Known issue [#16905](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/16905): An enabled built-in OpenHands skill can be absent from a new Claude Code ACP session. The enabled/disabled instruction-delivery check needs an approved authenticated Claude Code account, its ACP subprocess and the configured Code Review automation; no provider session is authorized here. (`F13.acp-conversation`).
- Known issue [#16296](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/16296): Claude Code credential fields remain visible below the already-connected banner, leading users to think keys are required. The connected-state check needs an approved existing Claude CLI login on the agent-server host; a dummy credential does not prove that signed-in state. (`F13.acp-credentials`).
- Known issue [#17051](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17051): Codex ACP can work in New Chat while Issue-to-PR automation fails with missing OpenAI API credentials. Reproduction needs an approved Codex subscription login plus a configured Issue-to-PR automation and its repository credentials; the report does not identify the saved automation/profile settings. (`F13.acp-conversation`).
- Known issue [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5167](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5167): On a headless Docker host an already usable Codex ChatGPT login can still time out during ACP authenticate. Reproduction needs an approved ChatGPT login in the reported headless/read-only-auth-file deployment and its adapter; a desktop or bogus login cannot establish this conditional trigger. (`F13.acp-conversation`).
- Known issue [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5995](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5995): Claude Code ACP first turns with `claude-opus-5-5` can fail because the pinned adapter bundles an older Claude Code. Blocked: needs an approved Claude login/API key entitled to Opus 5.5 and a real first turn; current SDK 1.55 still pins the reported adapter0.63.0. No authenticated turn was attempted. (`F13.acp-conversation`, `F13.acp-model-discovery`).
- Known issue [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5899](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5899): The browser tool can be reported unusable when genuine Chromium exists only under `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`. Blocked on this host: it has standard user Chrome. The distinguishing fixture needs a host/container with no standard/default-cache/PATH browser, plus a genuine custom-cache Chromium; never remove the user browser to create it. (`F13.openhands-options`; operational browser path F27).

# F14 — Secrets

Secrets are named values the agent can use during conversations. A user lists,
adds, edits and deletes them under Settings → Secrets; saved values are never
shown again, and every new conversation receives them as environment variables.

Source: `src/routes/secrets-settings.tsx`, `src/components/features/settings/secrets-settings/`, `src/api/secrets-service.ts`, `src/components/features/conversation/secret-request-card.tsx`, `src/services/secret-request.ts`, `src/stores/secret-request-store.ts`, `src/constants/secret-request.ts`, `src/api/request-secret-client-tool.ts`.

## Sub-features

- `F14.list`: the Secrets page lists each secret's name and description with Edit and Delete actions; the launcher-seeded `OPENHANDS_AUTOMATION_API_KEY` is always present.
- `F14.create`: adding a secret persists it; it is listed after a reload.
- `F14.create-validation`: duplicate names, names that break `^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_]{0,63}$` and empty values are refused with a message.
- `F14.edit`: editing the description with the value left blank keeps the stored value; Save stays disabled until something changes.
- `F14.delete`: deleting asks for confirmation; Cancel keeps the row, Confirm removes it for good.
- `F14.agent-access`: a conversation started after the secret was saved sees it as an environment variable.
- `F14.phone`: the page and its forms fit a 390 px viewport without horizontal overflow.
- `F14.form-back`: the Add and Edit forms replace the list with an **Add a Secret** / **Edit a Secret** title and a **Back** button; Back (like Cancel) returns to the list and discards the draft.
- `F14.rename`: the Edit form's name is editable; renaming with the value left blank keeps the stored value under the new name, and renaming onto an existing name is refused with `Secret already exists`.
- `F14.edit-value`: typing a value in the Edit form (labelled "Secret Value (leave blank to preserve the existing value)") replaces the stored value for new conversations.
- `F14.delete-escape`: Escape closes the delete confirmation without deleting.
- `F14.agent-request`: in a local conversation the agent's `request_secret` tool adds a **The agent needs a secret** card in the chat, right after the tool call, with its reason and the name prefilled; it does not block the conversation, so the agent can keep working and the user answers when ready. Add secret saves it, attaches it to the running conversation and reports `saved` to the agent, Cancel reports `not_saved`, and a name that is already saved is attached without a card. The value never reaches the agent's events.

## How to get to it (user POV)

- Sidebar settings gear (`backend-selector-settings-link`), then **Secrets** in the settings navigation (`sidebar-settings-/settings/secrets`).
- Direct URL `/settings/secrets`.
- Command menu (`Control+k` or `Meta+k`, or `command-menu-trigger` in the sidebar): search "Secrets", choose **Secrets settings**.
- The agent itself, in a conversation: its `request_secret` client tool adds the request card (`testid=secret-request-card`) to the chat on `/conversations/<id>` (`F14.agent-request`).

## Driving it with control-openhands

Preconditions:

- Baseline state (launched, doctored, `onboard --skip` done).
- No secret named `QA_TMP_SECRET`, `QA_AGENT_SECRET`, `QA_RENAMED_SECRET` or `QA_BACK_SECRET` exists (`control-openhands api GET /api/settings/secrets`).
- `F14.agent-access`, `F14.rename`, `F14.edit-value` and `F14.agent-request` need an active LLM profile (`control-openhands llm preset deepseek`).
- No secret named `QA_REQ_SECRET` or `QA_REQ_CANCEL` exists, for `F14.agent-request`.

- **Open the list (`F14.list`).** Navigate from the sidebar. Run `control-openhands browser click 'testid=backend-selector-settings-link'`, `control-openhands browser click 'testid=sidebar-settings-/settings/secrets'`, then `control-openhands browser count 'testid=secret-item >> has-text=OPENHANDS_AUTOMATION_API_KEY'`. The count is `1` and the URL is `/settings/secrets`.
- **Command-menu entry (`F14.list`).** Run `control-openhands browser goto /` (the previous bullet left `/settings/secrets`, which would make the URL check pass vacuously), then `control-openhands browser press Control+k`, `control-openhands browser type 'testid=command-menu >> role=combobox' Secrets`, `control-openhands browser press Enter`, then `control-openhands browser url`. The URL ends in `/settings/secrets`.
- **Create (`F14.create`).** Run `control-openhands browser click 'testid=add-secret-button'`, `control-openhands browser fill 'testid=add-secret-form >> testid=name-input' QA_TMP_SECRET`, `control-openhands browser fill 'testid=add-secret-form >> testid=value-input' dummy-value-123`, `control-openhands browser fill 'testid=add-secret-form >> testid=description-input' 'QA dummy'`, `control-openhands browser click 'testid=add-secret-form >> testid=submit-button'`, then `control-openhands browser reload` and `control-openhands browser count 'testid=secret-item >> has-text=QA_TMP_SECRET'`. The count is `1` after the reload.
- **Duplicate name (`F14.create-validation`).** Run `control-openhands browser click 'testid=add-secret-button'`, fill `name-input` with `QA_TMP_SECRET` and `value-input` with `other` as above, click `testid=add-secret-form >> testid=submit-button`, then `control-openhands browser snapshot 'testid=add-secret-form'`. The snapshot shows the paragraph `Secret already exists` and the form stays open. The paragraph uses the theme's danger colour (#18199): `control-openhands browser eval "getComputedStyle([...document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid=add-secret-form] p')].find(e=>e.innerText==='Secret already exists')).color"` is `rgb(231, 106, 94)` on OpenHands-Neutral and `rgb(209, 52, 56)` on Light+ (`F16.color-theme`).
- **Invalid name (`F14.create-validation`).** In the same form run `control-openhands browser fill 'testid=add-secret-form >> testid=name-input' 'bad name!'`, click submit, then `control-openhands browser eval "document.querySelector('[data-testid=add-secret-form] [data-testid=name-input]').validationMessage"`. The value is the browser's pattern message (`Please match the requested format.` in Chromium) and no secret is created (`api GET /api/settings/secrets`). Close with `control-openhands browser click 'testid=add-secret-form >> testid=cancel-button'`.
- **Empty value (`F14.create-validation`).** Run `control-openhands browser click 'testid=add-secret-button'`, fill `testid=add-secret-form >> testid=name-input` with `QA_EMPTY_VALUE` and leave `value-input` empty. `control-openhands browser enabled 'testid=add-secret-form >> testid=submit-button'` is `false`, and `control-openhands browser eval "document.querySelector('[data-testid=add-secret-form] [data-testid=value-input]').validationMessage"` is `Please fill out this field.` Close with `testid=add-secret-form >> testid=cancel-button`; `api GET /api/settings/secrets` lists no `QA_EMPTY_VALUE`.
- **Edit keeps the value (`F14.edit`).** Run `control-openhands browser click 'testid=secret-item >> has-text=QA_TMP_SECRET >> testid=edit-secret-button'`, `control-openhands browser value 'testid=edit-secret-form >> testid=value-input'` (empty) and `control-openhands browser enabled 'testid=edit-secret-form >> testid=submit-button'` (`false`). Fill `testid=edit-secret-form >> testid=description-input` with `QA dummy edited`; `enabled` turns `true`. Click `testid=edit-secret-form >> testid=submit-button`, `control-openhands browser reload`, then `control-openhands browser text 'testid=secret-item >> has-text=QA_TMP_SECRET'`. The row text is `QA_TMP_SECRET` and `QA dummy edited` separated by a tab (`"QA_TMP_SECRET\tQA dummy edited"` in the JSON output).
- **Delete with confirmation (`F14.delete`).** Run `control-openhands browser click 'testid=secret-item >> has-text=QA_TMP_SECRET >> testid=delete-secret-button'`; the dialog `testid=confirmation-modal` reads `Are you sure you want to delete this key?`. Run `control-openhands browser click 'testid=confirmation-modal >> testid=cancel-button'`; the row count stays `1`. Repeat the delete click, then `control-openhands browser click 'testid=confirmation-modal >> testid=confirm-button'`, `control-openhands browser reload` and `control-openhands browser count 'testid=secret-item >> has-text=QA_TMP_SECRET'`. The count is `0`.
- **Agent receives the secret (`F14.agent-access`).** Create `QA_AGENT_SECRET` with value `qa-dummy-4821` through the form as in Create. Run `control-openhands conversation start --prompt "Run exactly this command and reply with only its output: python3 -c \"import os; print(os.environ.get('QA_AGENT_SECRET') == 'qa-dummy-4821')\"" --wait --timeout 240`, then `control-openhands conversation events <id> --kinds ObservationEvent`. The terminal observation's text is `True`. Assert the observation, not the agent's reply: deepseek-flash often declines to echo anything about a secret (see Gotchas). Keep `QA_AGENT_SECRET` for Rename and Replace value below; they delete it.
- **Phone layout (`F14.phone`).** Run `control-openhands browser goto /settings/secrets` (`conversation start` left the browser on the conversation), `control-openhands browser viewport phone`, `control-openhands browser bbox 'testid=secrets-settings-screen'` and `control-openhands browser screenshot --feature F14.phone --name list`. `insideViewport` is `true` and `pageHorizontalOverflow` is `false`; the screenshot shows the table with Edit and Delete icons. Then `control-openhands browser click 'testid=add-secret-button'`, `control-openhands browser bbox 'testid=add-secret-form'` (`insideViewport` `true`, no page overflow) and `control-openhands browser screenshot --feature F14.phone --name add-form`; cancel the form. Return with `control-openhands browser viewport desktop`.
- **Back discards the draft (`F14.form-back`).** On `/settings/secrets` run `control-openhands browser click 'testid=add-secret-button'` and `control-openhands browser text 'testid=secret-editor-title'` (`Add a Secret`). Fill `testid=add-secret-form >> testid=name-input` with `QA_BACK_SECRET` and `value-input` with `dummy`, then `control-openhands browser click 'testid=back-to-secrets'`. `control-openhands browser count 'testid=add-secret-form'` is `0`, the list is back (`browser count 'testid=secret-item'` > `0`) and `control-openhands api GET /api/settings/secrets` lists no `QA_BACK_SECRET`. Reopening Add shows an empty `name-input` (`browser value`); leave with `testid=back-to-secrets`. The Edit form shows `Edit a Secret` in the same `secret-editor-title`.
- **Rename keeps the value (`F14.rename`).** Needs `QA_AGENT_SECRET` from Agent receives the secret. Run `control-openhands browser goto /settings/secrets`, `control-openhands browser click 'testid=secret-item >> has-text=QA_AGENT_SECRET >> testid=edit-secret-button'`, fill `testid=edit-secret-form >> testid=name-input` with `OPENHANDS_AUTOMATION_API_KEY` and click `testid=edit-secret-form >> testid=submit-button`: `control-openhands browser snapshot 'testid=edit-secret-form'` shows the paragraph `Secret already exists` and the form stays open. Fill `name-input` with `QA_RENAMED_SECRET` (value left blank), click submit, `control-openhands browser reload`; `browser count 'testid=secret-item >> has-text=QA_RENAMED_SECRET'` is `1`, the `QA_AGENT_SECRET` count is `0`, and `api GET /api/settings/secrets` lists only the new name. Then run `control-openhands conversation start --prompt "Run exactly this command and reply with only its output: python3 -c \"import os; print(os.environ.get('QA_RENAMED_SECRET') == 'qa-dummy-4821', 'QA_AGENT_SECRET' in os.environ)\"" --wait --timeout 240` and `control-openhands conversation events <id> --kinds ObservationEvent`: the observation is `True False`.
- **Replace the value (`F14.edit-value`).** Run `control-openhands browser goto /settings/secrets`, `control-openhands browser click 'testid=secret-item >> has-text=QA_RENAMED_SECRET >> testid=edit-secret-button'` and `control-openhands browser snapshot 'testid=edit-secret-form'` (the value textbox is named `Secret Value (leave blank to preserve the existing value)`). Fill `testid=edit-secret-form >> testid=value-input` with `qa-dummy-7350`; `browser enabled 'testid=edit-secret-form >> testid=submit-button'` is `true`. Click submit; `browser count 'testid=edit-secret-form'` is `0`. Start a conversation with the prompt `Run exactly this command and reply with only its output: python3 -c "import os; print(os.environ.get('QA_RENAMED_SECRET') == 'qa-dummy-7350')"` (quoted as above) and read its `ObservationEvent`: `True`.
- **Agent requests a secret (`F14.agent-request`).** Run `control-openhands browser goto /`, then `control-openhands conversation start --prompt "Call the request_secret tool with name QA_REQ_SECRET and reason 'QA check: a dummy token for verification.' Do not run any other tools. After calling it, end your turn and wait." --wait --timeout 240` (prints `<req-id>`; it leaves the browser on the conversation). `control-openhands conversation events <req-id> --kinds ActionEvent,ObservationEvent` shows the `request_secret` action and the observation `Tool call dispatched to client.`; `control-openhands browser snapshot 'testid=secret-request-card'` reads `region "The agent needs a secret"`, the reason `QA check: a dummy token for verification.`, textbox `Name` holding `QA_REQ_SECRET`, `Value`, `Description Optional`, `Cancel` and `Add secret [disabled]` (`browser screenshot --feature F14.agent-request --name card`). The chat input stays usable while the card is pending, and `control-openhands browser reload` keeps the card with the name still prefilled. Run `control-openhands browser fill 'testid=secret-request-card >> testid=value-input' qa-dummy-5190` and `control-openhands browser click 'testid=secret-request-card >> testid=submit-button'`: the card disappears, `control-openhands api GET /api/settings/secrets` lists `QA_REQ_SECRET`, and after `control-openhands conversation wait <req-id> --fresh --timeout 180` `control-openhands conversation events <req-id> --kinds MessageEvent` holds the user message `[secret-request] {"status":"saved","name":"QA_REQ_SECRET"}`, which the chat does not show (`browser count 'text=[secret-request]'` is `0`). The running conversation now has the value: `control-openhands conversation send <req-id> --prompt "Run exactly this command and reply with only its output: python3 -c \"import os; print(os.environ.get('QA_REQ_SECRET') == 'qa-dummy-5190')\"" --wait --timeout 240`, then the last terminal `ObservationEvent` is `True`. Cancel: `browser goto /`, start a second conversation with the same prompt naming `QA_REQ_CANCEL` and reason `QA cancel check.`, fill `value-input` with `should-not-save` and `control-openhands browser click 'testid=secret-request-card >> testid=cancel-button'`: the card disappears, `api GET /api/settings/secrets` lists no `QA_REQ_CANCEL`, the agent receives `[secret-request] {"status":"not_saved","name":"QA_REQ_CANCEL","guidance":...}`, and a reload does not bring the card back. Already saved: a third conversation asking for `QA_REQ_SECRET` again shows no card (`browser count 'testid=secret-request-card'` `0`) and its events hold `[secret-request] {"status":"saved","name":"QA_REQ_SECRET"}`. Expected: at phone width the card fits the chat column (`insideViewport` `true`) with the title, every field and both buttons visible; run the block below. Return with `browser viewport desktop`. `QA_REQ_SECRET` is deleted in the cleanup below.

  ```sh
  control-openhands browser viewport desktop
  control-openhands browser goto /
  control-openhands conversation start --prompt "Call the request_secret tool with name QA_REQ_PHONE and reason 'QA phone check.' Do not run any other tools. After calling it, end your turn and wait." --wait --timeout 240
  control-openhands browser wait 'testid=secret-request-card'
  control-openhands browser viewport phone
  control-openhands browser screenshot --feature F14.agent-request --name phone-width
  control-openhands assert --field insideViewport --equals true -- browser bbox 'testid=secret-request-card'
  control-openhands browser click 'testid=secret-request-card >> role=button[name="Cancel"]'
  control-openhands browser wait 'testid=secret-request-card' --state detached
  ```
- **Escape cancels delete (`F14.delete-escape`).** Run `control-openhands browser goto /settings/secrets`, `control-openhands browser click 'testid=secret-item >> has-text=QA_RENAMED_SECRET >> testid=delete-secret-button'`, `control-openhands browser press Escape`, then `control-openhands browser count 'testid=confirmation-modal'` (`0`) and `browser count 'testid=secret-item >> has-text=QA_RENAMED_SECRET'` (`1`). Clean up: delete `QA_RENAMED_SECRET` and then `QA_REQ_SECRET` (from `F14.agent-request`), each with `delete-secret-button` → `testid=confirmation-modal >> testid=confirm-button`, `browser reload`; `api GET /api/settings/secrets` lists only `OPENHANDS_AUTOMATION_API_KEY`.

- **Cipher mismatch refuses mutation (`F14.create`, `F14.edit`, `F14.delete`).** This is an external-state fixture, not a credential test. Arrange two own dummy secrets and a dummy loopback LLM key; privately back up the run-owned `encryption-key`, `settings.json` and `secrets.json`. Replace only the own cipher file with a newly generated value (never display it), restart and doctor. After bootstrap, restore the old encrypted store bytes under the replacement cipher to isolate the UI write. Add a new dummy secret through the real Secrets form, and inspect only boolean preservation metadata / availability of the old dummy value privately. Independently restore the encrypted settings baseline and change Sound Notifications through Application → Save. Expected: reject writes when existing encrypted state cannot decrypt, preserving it. Known failure, reproduced 2026-10-12 ([OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5622](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5622)): the secret create succeeds and rewrites an old entry while its dummy value is unavailable (getter 404, name still listed); two unrelated settings saves persist the old LLM key as null. Repeat with a fresh replacement cipher. Immediately restore the original cipher and both stores in `finally`, restart and doctor; original state must be readable again. This drives secret creation and settings Save, not every edit/delete permutation. Keep all cipher bytes, values and raw store snapshots private.

## Gotchas

- Settings nav test ids embed the route, slashes included: `sidebar-settings-/settings/secrets`. Quote the selector as written.

- The value editor is a plain `textarea`, not a password field: use dummy values only, and never ask the agent to print a real secret.
- Edit forms intentionally show an empty value; that is not data loss.
- The invalid-name check is native browser validation. It shows a tooltip that screenshots do not capture, and it leaves any earlier `Secret already exists` paragraph on screen. Assert with `validationMessage` and the API, not the paragraph.
- The model is the weak link in the agent checks, not the product: asked to print a secret's length or last characters, deepseek-flash replies "I can't run that one" and runs nothing, and even for the equality check it may refuse to repeat `True` in its reply. Use the equality prompt and read the terminal `ObservationEvent`; `conversation events` truncates message text to about 160 characters.
- The conversation Overview has no Secrets entry point: its "..." menu (`conversation-overview-ellipsis`) offers Workspace and Git sections only.
- There is no empty state to reach safely: `secrets-empty` renders only with zero secrets, which means deleting the launcher-seeded key (see below).
- Secrets saved in Settings reach only conversations started after the save. Reuse an older conversation and the variable is missing. Only `request_secret` (`F14.agent-request`) attaches a secret to a running conversation, and only on a local backend.
- `request_secret` is registered on every new OpenHands-agent conversation this frontend launches (not on ACP agents or older conversations) and appears in Show Agent Tools & Metadata (see `F07.agent-tools-modal`). The agent learns the outcome from a hidden `[secret-request] ...` user message; read it with `conversation events <id> --kinds MessageEvent`, not from the chat.
- At 390 px the name column truncates long names (`OPEN…`); use `browser text` on the row rather than the screenshot to read a name.
- `OPENHANDS_AUTOMATION_API_KEY` is seeded by the launcher for automations; deleting it breaks F18/F19 runs in the same stack.
- Known issue [#17710](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17710): On the Cloud backend, deleting a secret reportedly adds a suffixed duplicate and leaves the original. Reproduction needs a disposable writable OpenHands Cloud account at the affected service; Local secret CRUD exercises a different transport. (`F14.delete`, `F14.edit`).
